events.title: The First Council of Nicaea closes
events.description: By tradition the council summoned by Constantine ended on this date. It had condemned Arianism, adopted the Nicene Creed and set rules for dating Easter, shaping Christian doctrine for centuries.

events.title: Galileo demonstrates his telescope to Venice's rulers
events.description: Galileo showed the Venetian authorities his improved telescope, which made distant ships visible hours before they could be seen by eye. The Republic rewarded him with a lifetime post at Padua.

events.title: Uruguay declares independence from Brazil
events.description: A congress at Florida declared the Banda Oriental independent of the Empire of Brazil and united with the River Plate provinces. After a war, Uruguay became a sovereign state under the 1828 treaty.

events.title: First daily international scheduled air service begins
events.description: Aircraft Transport and Travel began daily flights between London's Hounslow Heath and Paris, carrying passengers, mail and goods. It was the start of scheduled international commercial aviation.
events.html: Aircraft Transport and Travel began daily flights between London's Hounslow Heath and Paris, carrying passengers, mail and goods. It was the start of scheduled international commercial aviation.

events.title: Paris is liberated from German occupation
events.description: French and American troops entered Paris and the German commander, General von Choltitz, surrendered, having ignored Hitler's order to destroy the city. De Gaulle led a victory march the next day.

events.title: Neil Armstrong dies aged 82
events.description: Neil Armstrong, the first person to walk on the Moon, died in Cincinnati after heart surgery. A modest engineer, he largely avoided the celebrity that followed Apollo 11.
